text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** Nearly every source I found agrees, and nearly all current power stations already use it.

## LiFePO4 vs NMC

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Cycle life** | Usually 2,000-6,000 cycles | Usually 500-1,000 (one source says up to 2,000) |
| **Failure behavior** | Milder: cooler, no flames in a lab overcharge test | More violent: flames and much higher peak temperatures |
| **Weight** | A bit heavier per Wh | Lighter cells, but the gap is smaller in finished units |
| **Price** | Median about $0.55/Wh in one dataset | Median about $0.95/Wh in the same dataset |
| **Cold charging** | Generally won't charge below 32°F | Same, per the manuals one source checked |

## Points to know

- **Cycle life matters most if you use it daily.** At one cycle a day, 500 cycles lasts about 1.4 years and 3,000 lasts about 8 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). For a few outages a year, either chemistry will age out from time before it runs out of cycles ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **The weight advantage of NMC is smaller than claimed.** At the cell level NMC is clearly denser. In finished stations, the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. OutageMath found only about a 10% gap in median Wh per pound, and its same-maker pairs showed the LFP version slightly heavier per kWh. Other sites claim 20-30%, so compare the specific models.
- **LFP is safer, but not fireproof.** In a lab overcharge test, LFP failed more mildly. It also reached thermal runaway earlier than NMC, and the Department of Energy notes LFP systems have had incidents too ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). I'd discount claims like "virtually impossible to catch fire."
- **Check the cycle rating's end point.** "3,000 cycles to 80%" promises more than "4,000 cycles to 70%," so compare like with like ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Cold weather depends on the maker.** Read the charging temperature range in the manual rather than assuming from the chemistry ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

## When NMC makes sense

Only for a small, lightweight unit you'll use lightly, or a heavily discounted clearance unit. If the listing doesn't name the chemistry, check the spec sheet. Some makers leave it out.

## An LiFePO4 example for home backup

The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating (to 80%) and a 5-year warranty. It's priced at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, as of the site's cart test on 2026-10-24. It isn't expandable, and it weighs 24.2 kg (about 53 lb). The listing says it suits backing up a fridge, router and lights for a day or two.
